Sodium was a massively multiplayer online game that was based in and exclusive to the PlayStation 3's online community-based social gaming network PlayStation Home. Sodium was a planned four-part series of games, only two of which were released by the time of Home's closure. It was developed by Outso, a developing company that developed spaces and content for Home, and it was published by Lockwood Publishing, who had published other content for Home. The first part, Sodium One, was released on December 17, 2009 to the European and North American versions of Home.[1] It was later released in the Japanese and Asian versions on June 17, 2010 and July 29, 2010 respectively. The second part, Sodium 2: Project Velocity, was released on June 16, 2011 to the European and North American versions of Home.[2]

Due to the nature of Home, the game continued to grow and expand as Home did. New games, virtual items, and community events were continually added until November 2014 when new content ceased to be published for Home, and Home closed on March 31, 2015.[3]

Sodium era un juego multijugador masivo en línea ambientado en PlayStation Home, la red social de juegos basada en comunidades de PlayStation 3, y exclusivo de ella. Sodium iba a ser una serie planificada de cuatro partes, de las cuales solo dos se lanzaron antes del cierre de Home. Fue desarrollado por Outso, una empresa que creaba espacios y contenido para Home, y publicado por Lockwood Publishing, que ya había publicado otro contenido para Home. La primera parte, Sodium One, se lanzó el 17 de diciembre de 2009 para las versiones europea y norteamericana de Home.[1] Posteriormente se lanzó para las versiones japonesa y asiática el 17 de junio de 2010 y el 29 de julio de 2010, respectivamente. La segunda parte, Sodium 2: Project Velocity, se lanzó el 16 de junio de 2011 para las versiones europea y norteamericana de Home.[2]

Debido a la naturaleza de Home, el juego siguió creciendo y expandiéndose a la par que Home. Se añadieron constantemente nuevos juegos, objetos virtuales y eventos comunitarios hasta noviembre de 2014, cuando dejó de publicarse contenido nuevo para Home, y Home cerró el 31 de marzo de 2015.[3]
